subject: science

entries: Temperature: molecules jiggle faster when hotter - turning the dial from 300 K to 600 K makes the same molecules jiggle harder, because their average kinetic energy (3/2) k T has doubled.
slots.label: Temperature: molecules jiggle faster when hotter
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Conduction: heat travels atom by atom - hot-end atoms vibrate strongly, collide with neighbours and pass the energy along the lattice (and, in metals, through free electrons) until the far end warms.
slots.label: Conduction: heat travels atom by atom
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Convection: the fluid loops - fluid heated at the bottom expands, grows less dense and rises, while cooler denser fluid sinks, so the circulating loop carries the heat around.
slots.label: Convection: the fluid loops
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Radiation: hotter means more packets, faster - every body radiates, and by P = sigma A T^4 doubling the kelvin temperature multiplies the radiated power by 16.
slots.label: Radiation: hotter means more packets, faster
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Misconception: a common mistake about heat and temperature - heat is the total over all molecules while temperature is the average per molecule, so a small hot cup can beat a big warm bucket on temperature while losing on total heat.
slots.label: Misconception: a common mistake about heat and temperature
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a substance: average KE = (3/2) k T, so temperature is proportional to that average when T is in kelvin.
slots.label: Temperature
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The model that treats a gas as a huge number of tiny particles in constant random motion, colliding elastically with each other and with the walls; pressure is the effect of those wall collisions.
slots.label: Kinetic theory
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder one because of their temperature difference; it is a transfer, not something a body contains.
slots.label: Heat
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The total kinetic energy of the molecules from their random motion plus their potential energy from intermolecular forces - the sum over every molecule, not the average.
slots.label: Internal energy
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Heat transfer through a material by particle collisions and vibrations passed on atom by atom, helped in metals by free electrons, with no bulk movement of the material.
slots.label: Conduction
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Heat transfer in a fluid by bulk movement: warmed fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises, while cooler denser fluid sinks, setting up a circulating loop.
slots.label: Convection
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves (mainly infrared), needing no medium; a black body radiates power P = sigma A T^4 by the Stefan-Boltzmann law.
slots.label: Radiation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A gas that obeys pV = nRT at all temperatures and pressures: its particles have negligible volume, exert no intermolecular forces except during collisions, and collide elastically.
slots.label: Ideal gas
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
